name: Question 11
problem: Consider the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 3 \\ 3 & 5\end{aligned}]$ and the quadratic curve ${x}^{T}\,Ax=3.$ Given that $A$ has eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=6$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=-4,$ find the principal axes of the curve.
worked_solution:
Notice that $A$ is symmetric. 
The principal axes of the curve 

$$
{x}^{T}\,Ax=3
$$

are the vectors that give an orthonormal eigenvector basis for $A.$ Let's now find these eigenvectors.

- For ${\lambda }_{1}=6,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-6I & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 3 \\ 3 & 5\end{aligned}]-6[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-9 & 3 \\ 3 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-6I)x=0$ gives the eigenvector ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}].$ Dividing ${v}_{1}$ by its norm $‖{v}_{1}‖=\sqrt{10},$ we get 

$$
\frac{{v}_{1}}{‖{v}_{1}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$

- For ${\lambda }_{2}=-4,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-(-4)I & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 3 \\ 3 & 5\end{aligned}]+4[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 3 & 9\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-(-4)I)x=0$ gives the eigenvector ${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$ Dividing ${v}_{2}$ by its norm $‖{v}_{2}‖=\sqrt{10},$ we get 

$$
\frac{{v}_{2}}{‖{v}_{2}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, the principal axes of our curve are

$\,$ $\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

Question 11

Consider the matrix A=[−3335] and the quadratic curve xTAx=3. Given that A has eigenvalues λ1=6 and λ2=−4, find the principal axes of the curve.

a
110[13] and 110[−31]
b
113[−23] and 113[32]
c
15[12] and 15[−21]
d
15[−23] and 15[32]
e
110[62] and 110[−26]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Notice that A is symmetric. The principal axes of the curve

xTAx=3

are the vectors that give an orthonormal eigenvector basis for A. Let's now find these eigenvectors.

  • For λ1=6, we have A−6I=[−3335]−6[1001]=[−933−1]. Seeking a non-zero solution of (A−6I)x=0 gives the eigenvector v1=[13]. Dividing v1 by its norm ‖v1‖=10, we get v1‖v1‖=110[13].

  • For λ2=−4, we have A−(−4)I=[−3335]+4[1001]=[1339]. Seeking a non-zero solution of (A−(−4)I)x=0 gives the eigenvector v2=[−31]. Dividing v2 by its norm ‖v2‖=10, we get v2‖v2‖=110[−31].

Therefore, the principal axes of our curve are

110[13] and 110[−31].
